Select the MTD of an iBOIN Trial

Source: R/iboin_select_mtd.R
iboin_select_mtd.Rd

Select the maximum tolerated dose from the final data of one or more trials of the iBOIN design of Zhou et al. (2021), with or without the prior information in the estimates of the DLT probabilities.

Usage

iboin_select_mtd(
  n_pts,
  n_tox,
  target,
  skeleton,
  prior_ess,
  with_prior = TRUE,
  cutoff_eli = 0.95,
  extrasafe = FALSE,
  offset = 0.05,
  robust = FALSE,
  min_mtd_sample = 1
)

Arguments

n_pts

Integer vector or matrix. Number of patients treated at each dose. A matrix holds one trial per row.

n_tox

Integer vector or matrix of the same shape. Number of DLTs observed at each dose.

target

Numeric scalar. Target DLT probability.

skeleton

Numeric vector, one value per dose. Prior DLT probability at each dose.

prior_ess

Whole number or vector of whole numbers, one per dose. Prior effective sample size.

with_prior

Logical scalar. When TRUE, the default, the prior information is added to the data before the isotonic regression. When FALSE the selection is that of boin_select_mtd.

cutoff_eli

Numeric scalar. Posterior probability cutoff for dose elimination. Defaults to 0.95.

extrasafe

Logical scalar. Apply the stricter safety stopping rule at the lowest dose. Defaults to FALSE.

offset

Numeric scalar between 0 and 0.5. Amount by which cutoff_eli is relaxed for the safety stopping rule. Defaults to 0.05.

robust

Logical scalar. Use the robust prior, see iboin_boundary. Defaults to FALSE.

min_mtd_sample

Integer scalar. Smallest number of patients a dose must have been given to be selected. Defaults to 1.

Value

A data frame with one row per trial and the columns trial, mtd (the selected dose, NA when none is selected) and reason ("selected", "lowest_dose_eliminated" or "no_admissible_dose").

Details

The article gives two estimates of the DLT probability of a dose for the selection of the MTD: the observed rate n_tox / n_pts, and the rate with the prior information, (n_tox + prior_ess * skeleton) / (n_pts + prior_ess). Either is made monotone by isotonic regression, and the dose whose estimate is closest to the target is selected. With with_prior = TRUE the numbers n_tox + prior_ess * skeleton and n_pts + prior_ess take the place of the DLTs and the patients in the estimate of boin_select_mtd; the doses that can be selected are still those that have been given to patients and are not eliminated, and the elimination uses the data alone, under a uniform prior.

The article does not say which estimate its simulation study uses. Its operating characteristics (Table S.1 of its supporting information) are reproduced with the prior information and not without it, see inst/reproduce/reproduce_Zhou2021.R. The estimate with the prior selects the true MTD more often when the prior MTD is right and less often when it is wrong.

References

Zhou, Y., Lee, J. J., Wang, S., Bailey, S. and Yuan, Y. (2021). Incorporating historical information to improve phase I clinical trials. Pharmaceutical Statistics, 20, 1017-1034. doi:10.1002/pst.2121

See also

sim_iboin, boin_select_mtd

Examples

skeleton <- c(0.10, 0.19, 0.30, 0.42, 0.54)
n_pts <- c(3, 6, 12, 9, 0)
n_tox <- c(0, 1, 3, 4, 0)

iboin_select_mtd(n_pts, n_tox, target = 0.30, skeleton = skeleton,
                 prior_ess = 3)
#>   trial mtd   reason
#> 1     1   3 selected
iboin_select_mtd(n_pts, n_tox, target = 0.30, skeleton = skeleton,
                 prior_ess = 3, with_prior = FALSE)
#>   trial mtd   reason
#> 1     1   3 selected
